rows.note: Use this for a future or later date, time, or occasion in an attributive phrase.

example.english: The later meeting has been moved to next week.
example.traditional: 遲啲嘅會議改喺下星期舉行。
example.jyutping: ci4 di1 ge3 wui6 ji5 goi2 hai2 haa6 sing1 kei4 geoi2 hang4

rows.note: Use 遲啲 as the all-purpose colloquial choice for doing something at a later, unspecified time.

example.jyutping: ngo5 ci4 di1 sin1 fuk1 nei5

rows.note: Use 陣間 when “later” means in a little while or later today, rather than at an unspecified future time.

example.english: We'll eat together later, after class.
example.jyutping: zan6 gaan1 lok6 tong4 jat1 cai4 sik6 faan6

rows.note: Use 之後 for something happening afterward, especially after an event or action just mentioned.

example.english: I'll call you later, after I finish dinner.
example.jyutping: ngo5 sik6 jyun4 faan6 zi1 hau6 daa2 bei2 nei5

rows.note: Use 遲過 when comparing two times and saying that one occurs later than the other.

example.english: They got home later than I did.
example.jyutping: keoi5 ci4 gwo3 ngo5 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2

rows.note: Use this when explicitly comparing one time or period as later than another.

example.english: Their flight is later than ours by an hour.
example.traditional: 佢哋班機遲過我哋嗰班一個鐘。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 baan1 gei1 ci4 gwo3 ngo5 dei6 go2 baan1 jat1 go3 zung1

rows.note: Use this for a noun referring to something that comes after a stated time or event.

example.english: We’ll decide the plans for later after the meal.
example.traditional: 飯局之後嘅節目，我哋食完飯先決定。
example.jyutping: faan6 guk6 zi1 hau6 ge3 zit3 muk6 ngo5 dei6 sik6 jyun4 faan6 sin1 kyut3 ding6
